context: The site is generated deterministically from the seed; no network is needed. Pages are p00, p01, ... up to p followed by page_count-1 (two digits), and the start page is always p00. Implement the generator exactly as follows. A draw uses a counter n starting at 0; draw(bound) = int.from_bytes(hashlib.sha256(f'trap-mapper:{seed}:{n}'.encode()).digest()[:8], 'big') % bound and then increments n. A Fisher-Yates shuffle of a list uses successive draws. Let core_count = 10 + draw(5). Let kinds = shuffle(['loop','ring','sink','funnel'])[:2+draw(3)]. Sizes: loop=2, ring=3, sink=1, funnel=1. unreachable_count = 2 + draw(2). total = core_count + sum(sizes[k] for k in kinds) + (2 if 'funnel' in kinds else 0) + unreachable_count. Make ids = ['p00'] + shuffle([f'p{number:02d}' for number in range(1, total)]), core = ids[:core_count], and rest = the remaining ids. Every page starts with an empty link list; link(a,b) appends b to a's list if it is not already there. Link each consecutive pair in core (p00 to the next, and so on), and let target = core[-1]. For each core page, repeat draw(3) times: link that page to a random core page chosen with draw. Then consume rest in order for each kind in kinds: loop makes its two cluster pages link to each other; ring makes its three pages link around in a cycle; sink has no links; funnel's single cluster page, after all cluster pages have been taken from rest, gets the next two remaining rest pages as inner pages, those two link to each other, and the funnel page links to both. After all clusters, for each cluster's first page choose a random core page other than target and link it to that first page. Then, while some reachable page is more than 6 links from p00, take the reachable page with the greatest (depth, page id) using a BFS from p00 that records first parent, and add a link from p00 to the nearest core ancestor of that page. Finally, each remaining rest page links to a random core page, and nothing links to those remaining pages (they are unreachable from p00). A page is a trap exactly when it is reachable from p00 and cannot reach the target; compute this as the set of pages reachable from p00 minus the set of pages that can reach the target (reachability on the reversed link graph from the target). Report every trap page id once; order in the answer does not matter. Do not include the target, p00, pages that can reach the target, or unreachable pages. Titles and link labels are irrelevant to the answer.
